To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the profitability of SEE banks is determined by bank specific, industry and macroeconomic variables, and that bank specific variables are the most important.

(1) the bank specific determinants of bank profitability, except liquidity, have the expected sign and are significant; (2) the macroeconomic variables have an ambiguous impact; and (3) the industry related variable, bank concentration, is significant and positively associated with bank profitability.
1. Bank size, bank capital and the efficiency of the loan portfolio have positive and statistically significant effects on bank profitability.

the determinants of profitability in the South Eastern European (CEE) region, using an un-balanced panel dataset of SEE credit institutions over the 1998 2 2002 period.
the determinants of profitability in a region where there is a lack of research in the area of bank profitability and where banking sector reforms are in the process of being implemented.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
bank specific determinants, particularly size and liquidity, are important determinants of bank profitability, whilst the macroeconomic determinant of inflation is a negative factor.
, in the short term, the SEE banking sector is still not fully liberalized and competitive, but the process of liberalization is well on its way and is likely to be completed in the near future.

bank specific determinants, in particular capital adequacy, size and liquidity, are the most important drivers of bank profitability, whilst industry related factors, in particular concentration, and macroeconomic factors, in particular inflation and GDP growth, are also significant.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

bank specific factors are more important determinants of bank profitability in SEE than industry or macroeconomic factors, and that the results provide some support to the structure conduct performance paradigm.
bank profitability is positively related to bank size and concentration, whilst negatively related to the level of capitalisation and non-performing loans.
the profitability of SEE banks is mainly determined by bank specific factors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, while the banking sector of SEE is still in the early stages of its development, the results obtained in this study are consistent with those found for more mature banking sectors.
the SEE banking sector is in the midst of a transition process that is not yet complete.

the profitability of the banking sector in SEE is not driven by the banking reforms undertaken, but by the structure of the banking system, which in turn depends on the degree of market concentration, and the level of competition.
